level1.text: A lamp at the bottom of a swimming pool sends light towards the water surface. The refractive index of water is $1.33$ and that of air $1.00$. What is the critical angle at the boundary between water and air?
The refractive index of diamond is $2.42$. What is the critical angle at the boundary between diamond and air?

The glass wall of an aquarium has a refractive index of $1.52$, and against its inner surface there is water with a refractive index of $1.33$. What is the critical angle when light goes from the glass into the water?

The refractive index of the glass of an optical fibre is $1.47$. What is the speed of light in the glass of the fibre? The speed of light in a vacuum is $3.00 \cdot 10^8\,\text{m/s}$. Give the answer in kilometres per second.
A light pulse travels in an optical fibre at the speed $2.0 \cdot 10^8\,\text{m/s}$. How long does it take the pulse to travel along a fibre $100\,\text{km}$ long? Give the answer in milliseconds.
A ray of light travels in a transparent substance towards its boundary with another transparent substance. In which situation is the ray totally internally reflected?
level1.answer: Light goes from a substance with a larger refractive index into one with a smaller refractive index, and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, so there is no refracted ray.

choices.text: Light goes from a substance with a smaller refractive index into one with a larger refractive index, and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, so the ray is refracted towards the normal.
choices.feedback: Wrong: when light goes from a substance with a smaller refractive index into one with a larger refractive index, the ray is refracted towards the normal, and a refracted ray exists at all angles of incidence. There is then no critical angle, so total internal reflection does not occur.

choices.text: Light goes from a substance with a larger refractive index into one with a smaller refractive index, and the angle of incidence is small, so the ray meets the boundary almost perpendicularly.
choices.feedback: Wrong: a ray that meets the boundary almost perpendicularly mostly goes through, and only a small part of it is reflected. Total internal reflection requires an angle of incidence larger than the critical angle, not a small angle of incidence.

choices.text: Light goes from a substance with a larger refractive index into one with a smaller refractive index, and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, so there is no refracted ray.
choices.feedback: Correct: light going from a substance with a larger refractive index into one with a smaller refractive index is refracted away from the normal. At the critical angle the angle of refraction is $90{}^\circ$, and at larger angles of incidence the law of refraction gives no angle of refraction, so all the light is reflected back.

choices.text: Light goes from air into any transparent substance, and the angle of incidence is large, so the boundary acts like a mirror.
choices.feedback: Wrong: light going from air into a substance is always partly refracted into the substance, however large the angle of incidence is. Total internal reflection requires that the light comes from a substance with a larger refractive index; no mirror surface is needed.

level1.text: The refractive index of an acrylic plate is $1.49$. The plate is under water, and the refractive index of water is $1.33$. What is the critical angle when light goes from the acrylic into the water?

The refractive index of the glass of an optical fibre is $1.45$. A light pulse travels along the axis of the fibre for $0.500\,\text{ms}$. How far does it travel in the fibre? The speed of light in a vacuum is $3.00 \cdot 10^8\,\text{m/s}$. Give the answer in kilometres.

level2.text: The refractive index of the core of an optical fibre is $1.47$, and the critical angle at the boundary between the core and the cladding is $82.0^\circ$. What is the refractive index of the cladding?

In binoculars light is turned by a glass prism whose cross-section is a right-angled isosceles triangle. The light enters the prism through the long side face and meets the short side face (the leg face) inside the prism at an angle of incidence of $45^\circ$, and it must be totally internally reflected from it. There is air outside the prism. What is the smallest refractive index the glass of the prism can have?

The critical angle at the boundary between a transparent plastic rod and air was measured to be $42.0^\circ$. What is the speed of light in the plastic? The speed of light in a vacuum is $3.00 \cdot 10^8\,\text{m/s}$. Give the answer in kilometres per second.

An optical fibre between two cities is $250\,\text{km}$ long, and the refractive index of the glass of the fibre is $1.46$. How long does it take a light pulse travelling along the axis of the fibre to travel from one city to the other? The speed of light in a vacuum is $3.00 \cdot 10^8\,\text{m/s}$. Give the answer in milliseconds.

A student investigates the refractive index of a piece of transparent plastic. The student shines a laser on the surface between the inside of the plastic and air and increases the angle of incidence until the refracted ray disappears. This angle of incidence is the critical angle $\alpha_\text{r}$. It is measured five times (example data).

Table values: the refractive index of acrylic is $1.49$ and that of polystyrene $1.59$. The refractive index of air is $1.00$.

a) Calculate the mean of the critical angle and, using it, the refractive index $n$ of the plastic.

b) Estimate the scatter of the series of measurements as half of the range and calculate the refractive indices corresponding to its extreme values. Which plastic is the piece most likely to be?

Give the result of part a) in the answer field.

data.caption: Critical angle between plastic and air in five measurements (example data)

level2.text:
The refractive index of the core of an optical fibre is $1.48$ and the length of the fibre is $10.0\,\text{km}$. A very short light pulse is sent into the beginning of the fibre, and at the other end of the fibre the intensity $I$ of the light arriving is measured as a function of the time $t$ counted from the moment of sending.

In the table the intensity is given as a percentage of the largest value (example data). The width of the pulse is the time from the first row of the table where $I$ is at least $50\,\%$ to the last such row.

a) Determine the width of the pulse from the table in nanoseconds.

b) Calculate the travel time of light travelling along the axis and compare it with the moment when the pulse begins to arrive according to the table. Explain why the pulse that arrives is wider than the one sent.

Give the result of part a) in the answer field.

data.caption: Intensity of the light arriving (example data)

level2.text:
A student solves a problem where light goes from air into glass ($n = 1.50$) at an angle of incidence of $70{}^\circ$ and the question is what happens to the light.

The student's solution: “The critical angle is $\alpha_\text{r} = \sin^{-1}(1.00 : 1.50) = 41.8{}^\circ$. The angle of incidence $70{}^\circ$ is larger than the critical angle, so the light is totally internally reflected and does not enter the glass.”

a) Explain what is wrong in the student's reasoning.

b) Calculate at what angle to the normal the light continues in the glass.

Give the result of part b) in the answer field.

level3.text: A small lamp is at the bottom of a swimming pool at a depth of $1.80\,\text{m}$. The refractive index of water is $1.33$. Seen from above the pool in the dark, light from the lamp comes out of the water surface only from a circular area whose centre is directly above the lamp. Outside the circle the surface looks dark. What is the radius of the circle?

The refractive index of the core of an optical fibre is $1.480$ and that of the cladding $1.460$. A short light pulse is sent into the fibre. Some of the light travels along the axis of the fibre, and some travels in a zigzag so that it meets the boundary between the core and the cladding exactly at the critical angle. How much later does the zigzagging light arrive at the end of a straight fibre $1.00\,\text{km}$ long than the light along the axis? The speed of light in a vacuum is $3.00 \cdot 10^8\,\text{m/s}$. Give the answer in nanoseconds.

A ray of light travelling in a bare glass rod ($n = 1.50$) meets the side of the rod at an angle of incidence of $60^\circ$. Against air the ray is totally internally reflected. However, a water drop ($n = 1.33$) sticks to the side of the rod exactly where the ray meets it. At what angle to the normal does the ray continue in the water drop?

The core of an optical fibre is glass, and it is surrounded by a cladding whose refractive index is slightly smaller. The fibre ends in a flat end face in air, whose refractive index is $1.00$.

Light stays in the core only if it is totally internally reflected at the boundary between the core and the cladding. Therefore light can meet the end face only up to the angle of incidence $\theta_\text{max}$, when the angle of incidence is measured from the axis of the fibre. This is the acceptance angle of the fibre.

The table gives the refractive indices of three types of fibre (example data).

a) Calculate the acceptance angle $\theta_\text{max}$ of fibre B. First find the largest angle at which a ray travelling in the core can meet the boundary between the core and the cladding, and deduce from it what angle the ray makes with the axis. Then refract the ray at the end face.

b) Calculate the acceptance angle also for fibres A and C.

c) The larger the difference between the refractive indices of the core and the cladding, the more light the fibre accepts, but the more the pulse spreads over a long distance. Justify this by calculating for the three fibres the number $\dfrac{n_1}{n_2} - 1$, which tells the relative delay of the zigzagging light compared with the light along the axis.

Give the result of part a) in the answer field.

The core of a plastic optical fibre has a diameter of $1.0\,\text{mm}$, the refractive index of the core is $1.49$ and that of the cladding $1.40$.

The fibre is bent into an arc of a circle of radius $R$ (measured to the centre line of the fibre). Before the bend a ray of light travels parallel to the axis of the fibre. In the bend it continues straight until it meets the boundary at the outer edge of the bend. The most dangerous is the ray that travels next to the inner edge of the core.

The table gives the power passing through the fibre when the fibre is bent to different radii (example data).

a) What is the angle of incidence of the ray at the outer boundary when it travels next to the inner edge? Draw a picture of the situation (you check the picture yourself) and justify: in the right-angled triangle of the picture there are the centre of the bend, the path of the ray and the radius of the outer edge. Express the sine of the angle of incidence in terms of $R$ and the radius of the core $a$.

b) Calculate the smallest bending radius $R_\text{min}$ at which even the most dangerous ray is still totally internally reflected.

c) Compare the result with the table. Explain why the power does not drop sharply to zero exactly at $R_\text{min}$.

Give only the result of part b) in the answer field, in millimetres.

data.caption: Power transmitted by the fibre as a function of the bending radius (example data)
